title: AegisPay post-incident playbook bridgecall
summary: Follow-up on last week's outage window, clarify mitigations, align on runbook/responsibilities, and agree pilot for dedicated capacity + regional fallback. Actionable next steps and an ask for logs/benchmarks from AegisPay.
topics: KV cache warmup and prefix caching
next_steps: Redwood to send annotated incident timeline and proposed playbook v1 (Maya) by 2025-08-15
AegisPay to share filtered kube and inference logs + request IDs for the outage window by 2025-08-14
Schedule a 90-minute pilot kickoff (dedicated pool) week of 2025-08-25 (Liam/Maya)
action_items: Maya Chen: send incident annotated timeline and playbook v1 (2025-08-15)
Kunal Mehta: export 2 hours of inference logs and prefix cache metrics (2025-08-14)
Liam O'Connor: prepare load-profile runbook and baseline benchmark script for AegisPay (2025-08-20)
Lina Ortiz: list required artifacts for compliance review (SOC2 scope) and share (2025-08-16)
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Sara (AegisPay SRE), Devon (CTO), Kunal (Infra), Lina (Security), Tom (Product)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): okay thank you all for joining. quick agenda — we want to recap the outage window, confirm the immediate mitigations you put in, and then walk through a proposed playbook plus next steps for the dedicated pilot. who wants to kick off from the AegisPay side?

[00:18] Sara (AegisPay): hi thanks. yeah so we had that spike last tuesday around 02:14 UTC that cascaded into request timeouts, backend queue backed up, and then some retries amplified it. we rolled back the canary and moved traffic to the fallback model but there was still about 12 minutes of elevated 5xx. we traced it to a cold-KV-cache pattern plus a burst of long context chat sessions that exceeded our typical seq len.

[00:43] Liam (Redwood): okay cold KV cache and long seqs — that matches some of what we saw. to be clear, the runtime was prioritizing batching which increased tail latency during the warmup because the auto-batcher held for enough tokens to make efficient throughput decisions. that mixed with prefix cache misses caused higher p99.

[01:10] Devon (AegisPay): can i stop you — when you say "prefix cache", is that the same as the KV cache / warmup you talked about in the doc? i'm still a little fuzzy on the distinction between prefix caching vs full session caching.

[01:25] Liam (Redwood): yes sorry terminology — in our notes prefix caching is the KV-level cache for reused prompt prefixes across requests. session caching includes per-connection kv for autoregressive decode. in your case both were impacted because many chats shared a similar system prompt but the session token windows were larger so misses were costly.

[01:50] Kunal (AegisPay): quick q — we saw a bunch of retries from our side when the gateway gave 503s and then client-side backoff retried immediately. we might have made it worse. any guidance on client side backoff pattern?

[02:05] Maya (Redwood): yeah good callouts. for high-concurrency clients we recommend jittered exponential backoff with a capped concurrency per user-id to avoid retry storms. we'll add explicit suggested values in the playbook.

[02:20] Sara (AegisPay): also security flagged that the outage overlapped with a secrets rotation, and we're double-checking there wasn't any KMS churn in the same window. that said, our audit logs didn't show errors but we want the playbook to include KMS sanity checks.

[02:40] Lina (AegisPay): right — i'll confirm. for SOC 2 purposes we need the timeline with ACL changes and who touched KMS. if there's any correlation that's important.

[02:55] Priya (Redwood CSM): noted — we'll make sure to call out KMS health probes as part of the readiness checklist.

[03:10] Tom (Product): from product side the big ask is: how do we guarantee 99.9 for the checkout flow? our tolerance for any human-facing latency above 400ms is low.

[03:25] Liam (Redwood): right, so two levers — dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to avoid noisy neighbors and predictable batching, and regional fallback where we route to a lower-cost lower-latency variant when sequences exceed threshold. dedicated gives you throughput SLOs but you still need prefix cache warmup strategy during traffic spikes.

[03:50] Devon (AegisPay): can you quantify the warmup period? like how many requests until cache steady-state?

[04:05] Liam (Redwood): it depends on distribution — for highly repeated prefixes steady state can be under 60s; for diverse sessions it might be minutes. in your traffic profile from July, we saw a bimodal distribution: 40% short chats, 10% very long sessions that cause bulk of tail cost.

[04:30] Sara (AegisPay): you mentioned autoscale burst earlier — does that help with warmup? we don't want to overprovision but we also don't want head-of-line stalls.

[04:45] Maya (Redwood): autoscale helps throughput but not instantaneous p99 if cache is cold. we recommend a combined approach: reserved dedicated baseline for critical routes + short-term burst capacity + prefix pre-warm on deploys/batch warmers during predictable peaks (e.g., marketing push).

[05:12] Kunal (AegisPay): what's the mechanism for pre-warming? can we send synthetic warmup traffic?

[05:20] Liam (Redwood): yes synthetic warmup is standard — we can provide a script that replays representative prefixes with short delays so kv-population happens before traffic hits prod. we'll include that script in the pilot repo.

[05:38] Sara (AegisPay): one of our concerns is risk transfer — if we move to dedicated, how does billing/commit work for burst and unused capacity? also, legal wants fallback plans that minimize liability while still meeting SLAs.

[05:55] Maya (Redwood): good question. dedicated is monthly reserved capacity, with burst credits you can consume beyond reserve; unused baseline credits don't carry financial penalty under our standard pilot terms. we'll share a sample term sheet. for liability, the playbook will include explicit runbook stages and communication points — e.g., when to fail open to a lower-tier model vs when to suppress features.

[06:22] Lina (AegisPay): legal will want to see audit trails for fallbacks — who initiated, timestamp, fallthrough reason. do you emit structured logs for those events?

[06:33] Liam (Redwood): yes we emit structured event logs: routing decision, policy id, model variant, latency breakdown. sometimes the export naming in our telemetry pipeline gets munged by third-party parsers, so we'll attach a legend in the playbook.

[06:50] Tom (Product): you earlier mentioned "hold for batching" behaviour increased tail latency — can we tune the batching window?

[06:58] Liam (Redwood): yes batching window and pack size are tunable per route. for interactive checkout flows we recommend a low hold-time and smaller batch sizes to keep p99 down even if unit cost increases slightly. you can measure cost delta in the console.

[07:18] Sara (AegisPay): let's be explicit in the playbook: route A (checkout) low-latency config, route B (analytics) throughput-optimized.

[07:26] Maya (Redwood): agreed. we'll draft route templates.

[07:35] Devon (AegisPay): about rollback — during the incident we reverted a canary which helped but didn't fully mitigate. any read on why fallback model still had higher error rates?

[07:50] Liam (Redwood): likely configuration mismatch — different quantization profile on the fallback model increased decode errors for long contexts. also, some of the metrics indicated tokenization differences which caused unexpected sequence expansions. we should standardize tokenizer/quant profile parity across model variants in your deploy pipeline.

[08:14] Kunal (AegisPay): we'll audit our deploys. can redwood do a quick parity check across model artifacts?

[08:21] Maya (Redwood): yes we can run a diff on model manifests and quant tables as part of the pilot preflight. Liam will own that step.

[08:33] Sara (AegisPay): on monitoring — our ops noticed that Redwood's console alerted on high queue depth but it was buried among other alerts. can you expose a critical path alert for our SRE?

[08:46] Priya (Redwood CSM): absolutely. we can provide a prebuilt PagerDuty integration and a critical alert template that hits your SRE rotation directly. we'll share the alertbook.

[09:00] Tom (Product): security again — SSO tokens restarted around the same time, could be coincidence but we need a checklist to rule out chained failures.

[09:12] Lina (AegisPay): yes that was our fear. we'll provide the SSO rotation log. if there's any correlation we'll raise a post-incident corrective.

[09:26] Maya (Redwood): ok noted. adding SSO/KMS correlation checks to playbook.

[09:34] Devon (AegisPay): can we go through the proposed playbook steps briefly?

[09:40] Liam (Redwood): sure — high level: 1) preflight (artifact parity, KMS probe, telemetry sanity), 2) warmup (synthetic prefixes), 3) route-level config (batching windows, quant parity), 4) autoscale policy & burst config, 5) fallback policy (model variant + routing), 6) incident communication plan (who messages customers, telemetry snapshot), 7) post-incident blameless RCA cadence.

[10:10] Sara (AegisPay): sounds good. on step 3, who verifies quant parity? automated or manual?

[10:18] Liam (Redwood): automated check + a manual sanity sample. we'll run an artifact diff and a short inference parity run with 200 sample prompts.

[10:30] Kunal (AegisPay): about the synthetic warmup, how much traffic do we need to emulate? we want minimal cost but meaningful warmup.

[10:38] Liam (Redwood): typically a 1-3% of expected peak for 5 minutes seeded across prefixes does the trick. we'll share tuned numbers based on your July traffic.

[10:50] Tom (Product): and for the pilot — what's the expected timeline?

[10:55] Maya (Redwood): propose pilot kickoff week of 2025-08-25, two-week baseline to collect telemetry, then configurable hardening sprint. so 3-4 weeks total for initial pilot.

[11:10] Devon (AegisPay): does the pilot require on-prem access or just VPC peering?

[11:18] Maya (Redwood): VPC peering is fine; private deployment isn't required for this pilot. dedicated pool in our hosted Dedicated offering with VPC peering will provide isolation.

[11:30] Lina (AegisPay): legal will want a narrow scope; can you provide a one-page pilot statement of work?

[11:38] Maya (Redwood): yes we will provide an SOW + pilot terms.

[11:45] Sara (AegisPay): latency SLOs — can you commit to p99 target for route A during the pilot or is it observational?

[11:55] Liam (Redwood): during pilot we provide best-effort SLO targets and telemetry. production SLA requires the reserved commit. pilot will provide measured p50/p95/p99 and recommended delta to hit 99.9 after commit.

[12:12] Kunal (AegisPay): another ops question — are there guardrails in the console to prevent accidental config changes that might disable caching?

[12:22] Priya (Redwood CSM): yes we have RBAC and change approvals. for Dedicated we can add an approval gate for route-critical config; we'll include recommended settings in the playbook.

[12:35] Tom (Product): any immediate quick wins we can do before pilot?

[12:40] Liam (Redwood): yes — reduce batching hold time on checkout route, enable prefix prewarm for the heavy prefixes, and tighten client retry backoff. low lift changes with measurable impact.

[12:55] Sara (AegisPay): perfect. we'll prioritize those.

[13:05] Maya (Redwood): ok last thing — for the incident timeline, we need those filtered logs and a short list of request IDs that showed the 5xx spike so we can correlate. Kunal are you able to pull that?

[13:17] Kunal (AegisPay): yes i'll pull 3-4 sample request IDs and the kube/system logs for the window; aiming to drop in s3 by 2025-08-14.

[13:28] Priya (Redwood CSM): i'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff once we agree on availability.

[13:35] Maya (Redwood): great. to close, recap of next steps: we (Redwood) send playbook + annotated timeline draft, AegisPay send logs + request IDs, we schedule pilot kickoff week of 8/25.

[13:48] Devon (AegisPay): thanks all. quick aside — are there cost estimates for Dedicated during pilot?

[13:55] Maya (Redwood): yes sample cost sheet coming with playbook.

[14:02] Sara (AegisPay): thanks — appreciate the concrete plan.

[14:08] Liam (Redwood): one last note: we saw "tokenization expansion" as a contributing factor; please include sample payloads in the logs so we can reproduce locally.

[14:18] Kunal (AegisPay): will do.

[14:25] Maya (Redwood): ok wrapping — thanks everyone, we'll follow up on items and close the loop in the thread.

[14:34] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns and acronyms may be misrecognized (e.g., KV cache -> K V cache, SSO token rotations), occasional false punctuation.
